systems.name: Logistics Exceptions: Designing Around a Policy Gate
systems.headline: One shipment. The Policy Gate decides.
systems.discoverySection: Let Each Answer Move a Box
systems.description: Combine fresh and batch carrier signals while an independent gate controls every automated resolution.
systems.question: A regional EU carrier reports shipment EU-42 with no scan since yesterday.
systems.scope: Follow an EU shipment from carrier signal to an authorised resolution or visible human queue. Shared logic does not move regional records.
systems.provenance: Architecture, requirements and boundaries are adapted from the named canonical Markdown. Scenario branches, identifiers and payloads are illustrative teaching examples, not executions or measured results. Source assumptions remain assumptions.

discovery.question: Data volume and freshness per carrier?
discovery.answer: The scenario assumes about 60% webhook carriers at 200 events/s peak and 40% batch carriers every 2–6 hours.
discovery.decision: Keep separate streaming and scheduled batch ingestion, then converge on one event model.

discovery.question: Who are the users, and what scale?
discovery.answer: The source assumes 150 ops agents, about 40 concurrent, across three shifts.
discovery.decision: Size for event throughput and correctness, not a huge interactive user count.

discovery.question: Where is the auto-resolve vs human-approval boundary?
discovery.answer: Under $500 and high confidence may auto-resolve. Customs/regulatory is always human; higher value or low confidence is human.
discovery.decision: Check customs first in a separate, testable Policy Gate. Clarify the exact $500 boundary before implementation.

discovery.question: Regional or multi-tenant topology?
discovery.answer: One customer spans US, EU and APAC; EU data cannot leave the EU.
discovery.decision: Share versioned logic and policy while keeping event stores and audit logs regional.

scenarios.label: EU batch missed scan, auto-resolved

stages.title: Accept the batch carrier’s actual freshness
stages.what: An EU carrier delivers a CSV four hours after its last file. Batch ingestion parses it and retains the source update times.
stages.why: Polling more often cannot make a carrier file fresher.

stages.title: Draft a resolution without executing it
stages.what: The agent proposes rescheduling a $320 shipment. It attaches an illustrative high-confidence score and the evidence behind the draft.
stages.why: The proposal must reach the independent Policy Gate before any action.
stages.next: Next: Check customs before value and confidence.

checks.text: A model confidence score does not authorise execution.

stages.title: Check customs before value and confidence
stages.what: This is not customs or regulatory work. The gate then checks value below $500 and confidence above the configured threshold, and permits this low-risk action.
stages.why: Reversing that order would allow a confident model to bypass customs review.
stages.next: Next: Open the carrier circuit after a timeout.

checks.text: Customs/regulatory always routes to a human first.

stages.title: Execute once with the carrier’s idempotency support
stages.what: The adapter sends the reschedule under one action idempotency key. This carrier confirms the new booking.
stages.why: A transient retry must not create a second booking.
stages.next: Next: Keep the decision and result in the EU audit log.

checks.text: Use an integration with authoritative idempotency support. The source routes unsupported legacy cases to humans.

stages.title: Keep the decision and result in the EU audit log
stages.what: The regional log records source freshness, gate rules, confidence, action key and carrier confirmation. The ops view shows the completed resolution.
stages.why: Correctness includes explaining why the system acted and where the data stayed.
stages.next: An ops reviewer approves the $700 reschedule, which the carrier confirms once.

checks.text: Monitor approval queues, circuit breakers and event backlog.

stages.why: Freshness changes ingestion latency, not the customs approval rule.

stages.component: Normalised event stream + Regional event store
stages.what: The validated customs webhook enters the normalised EU event stream. The event preserves its customs-hold type, and the event and shipment state remain in the EU region.

stages.title: Classify the customs hold
stages.what: Detection identifies a customs hold. The agent drafts the proposed next step and evidence, but cannot approve its own action.
stages.why: The exception type must survive into the gate input.
stages.next: Next: Short-circuit customs to a human.

checks.text: Carry the authoritative exception type; do not let a confidence score erase it.

stages.title: Short-circuit customs to a human
stages.what: The exception is a customs hold, even though the value is $320 and confidence is high. The first rule sends it to the approval queue.
stages.why: Customs is a hard boundary, not a score that can be outweighed.
stages.next: Next: Wait with the explanation visible.

checks.text: No automated execution follows a customs decision without a real human approval.

stages.component: Ops approval queue + Regional audit log
stages.what: The ops queue shows the customs rule, draft and evidence. No reviewer has approved, so the case stays pending in the EU audit trail.
stages.why: A pending approval is not successful resolution.
stages.next: The customs case is waiting for an ops reviewer. No carrier action has executed.

revision.pitch: I would start with the four clarifying answers because each changes the architecture. Carriers have both webhooks and scheduled files, so I would keep two intake paths and converge after normalisation. Batch detection stays late by design and the agent sees that freshness. Detection produces a typed exception, then a resolution agent drafts an action and confidence. A separate Policy Gate checks customs first: it always needs a human, regardless of value or confidence. Only non-customs cases under the value boundary and above the configured confidence threshold can auto-resolve. Higher risk becomes an explained ops draft. Carrier calls need least-privilege credentials, idempotency and circuit breakers. I would share versioned logic across regions but keep EU event data and audit logs in the EU. This is a low-user-count system where event throughput, approval capacity and correct actions matter more than concurrent chat sessions.
revision.flow: Webhook or batch → regional normalised stream → detect → draft → customs-first Policy Gate → authorised execution or human queue → regional audit
requirements: Ingest carrier events, detect disruptions, classify type/value/confidence, auto-resolve low-risk cases, route drafts for approve/edit/reject, and retain a full audit trail.
EU residency, reliable detection, low detection-to-draft latency, auditability, bounded cost and carrier onboarding without a core redeploy.
discovery: Data volume and freshness per carrier?
Who are the users, and what scale?
Where is the auto-resolve vs human-approval boundary?
revision.tradeoff: A separate Policy Gate costs a hop but makes the customs rule independently testable. Regional data planes preserve residency while making global reporting harder.
revision.failure: A carrier timeout does not prove failure or success. Preserve the action key, stop runaway retries and hand ambiguous completion to ops.
ops: Use queues and stateless detection. Watch event backlog and approval-queue capacity at shift handoff.
Track time-to-detect separately for batch and real-time carriers; a blended average hides the source delay.
Avoid pointless batch polling. Bound retries and degrade a failing carrier to human review.
Test customs before confidence, value-edge cases, duplicate actions, regional isolation and actual carrier idempotency support.
revision.remember: Check customs first. Share logic, isolate regional data.
